title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of member States to ratify and apply international labour standards and to fulfil their reporting obligations

description.narrative: China has made steady progress in application of international labour standards (ILS) through its laws and policies, banning child labour, forced labour and discrimination, and strengthening occupational safety and health. However, gaps remain in legislative alignment and implementation, and knowledge of ILS is uneven among tripartite constituents at national and local levels. To support tripartite constituents in advancing the effective application of ratified international labour Conventions, ILO will provide tailored support to address practical challenges in implementing the ILS. This includes sustained support to align national legislations and policies, actions and practices with the observations and recommendations of ILO supervisory bodies. In 2026 and 2027, the ILO interventions will focus on strengthening the institutional and technical capacity of constituents to effectively apply ILS, particularly fundamental Conventions and Recommendations. Expected results include: Progress made by government and social partners in application of ratified Conventions in line with comments of ILO supervisory bodies; New and improved policies and actions promoting fundamental principles and rights at work.
